posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
I decided to play a solo game recently and felt like playing a powerful team, so chose Team Leader Tachyon, NightMist, O-X, and The Scholar. This was before I gave any consideration at all to which villain I'd be playing or in which environment. After crushing Citizen Dawn, I thought to myself, "If I couldn't choose those four heroes, for some reason, who would I have chosen?"

 

I decided that I would have gone with Legacy, Tempest, and The Wraith for sure. I was a little unsure who to choose as my fourth, but eventually settled on Chrono-Ranger, figuring he would benefit really well from Legacy's boosts and thinking that he does a great job of building up.

 

Then I thought to myself, "Well, what if _THOSE_ four weren't available?" A much more difficult choice loomed. I started with Visionary and fairly quickly added Ra, to make sure I had some damage dealing I could do. I decided to round out the team w/ Haka and Fanatic. it was by no means an easy choice, but I felt that gave my team tons and tons of damage with good deck control and at least the possibility of ongoing destruction.

 

Realizing there were only six heroes unchosen, I began to wonder which two would be left out of a final team? Thinking through my fourth squad I decided I definitely wanted Argent Adept and Unity. They're both strong, but slow-build heroes that I feel have definite weaknesses. Still, they can work really well together. Who would get the last two spots? I decided I needed some consistent damage dealers, so while Expatriette _might_ have trouble starting with a gun, as long as she did, she'd be perfect. Then I threw in Bunker, also for the damage he can do.

 

The heroes left out? Mr. Fixer and Absolute Zero. Absolute Zero almost snuck on to the second team w/ Legacy, and almost made it on to the fourth team because of his ongoing destruction. Mr. Fixer? Not sure what to say. I really like Mr. Fixer and there are times when he is the reason the heroes win, but I just don't see myself ever picking him because I think he's going to be a better choice than other heroes at increasing the odds of winning.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
Hmmm... I think i'm going to copy you Arenson9. First I have to give it some thought, lucky for you guys my thought won't seem as long as it actually was.

 

My first team would be Argent Adept, Absolute Zero, Tachyon, and Mister Fixer. I've got Absolute Zero there for the major damage dealer, with Fixer being back up. Also Fixer can take the role as a tank if need be and the AoE giver when needed. Argent Would be help AZ get to his stuff significantly quicker, while also allowing Tachyon to burn through her deck. Tachyon will be there for the killing blow, as AZ probably won't last too long, but just long enough and able to deal enough that Tachyon should be able to get 40+ damage in a turn. Also ongoing and environment destruction would be no problem.

 

Next up... I'd say Legacy, Fanatic, Tempest, and Expatriette. Fanatic, Tempest, and Expat can really get the ball rolling with the damage. They also do multiple instances of damage in a round or large AoE, allowing them to take full advantage of Legacy's damage increase. Still lots of ongoing and environment destruction. There is also Legacy's tanking ability will help any hero that may start to fall behind a bit.

 

Now it's starting to get a little more difficult. I'd say... NightMist, Visionary, Haka, and... I'll go with Omnitron-X. NightMist and Haka will be used to lay on the damage. Visionary for her deck manipulation and damage altering powers to allow Omnitron-X to tank the villain character card with ease. Omnitron-X for mostly tanking and just putting loads of hero cards into play. Also between Visionary and Omnitron-X, there will be no unwanted ongoing or environment cards in play.

 

My final team; Wraith, Ra, Unity, and Chrono-Ranger. I'd have Wraith on deck manipulation, paired with Stun Bolt to lower the damage out put by the villain. Ra's Imbued Fire will help Chrono-Ranger do more damage, which is always good for him. Ra would totally be laying waste to the entire field, making sure no lesser minions are there blocking Chrono-Ranger's damage. Unity would clean up anything Ra didn't kill, while all extra damage would be targeted at the villain. While Chrono-Ranger of course will blasting chunks out of the the villain. This team however will have the hardest time dealing with Ongoing/Environment cards, but they make it up in Ra power.

 

That leaves Scholar and Bunker out in the cold. The major part of them being left out was because the lack of ongoing/environment destruction. Each of my teams only consist of 1 hero that lacks that. Meaning they would be filling the shoes of Fixer, Legacy, Haka, or Ra. The only one that almost made it was Bunker taking the place of Haka. To me Haka was the better choice, as he has Savage Mana, plus the lack of need cards in play to do damage.

well, more semi-on-topic. Do you look to bring the Nemesis when facing a certain Villain? I don't care for Omni-X when facing Omnitron, but I'm not leaving out Ra against Ennead, or Fanatic against Apostate.

I almost always make a deliberate decision about whether to use the nemeses or not, but I can go either way.  For the moment I only own the EE, so I don't have nems for Dawn or Omnitron. I've played Blade once with Legacy and once without him; I played Voss with Tempest and plan to play without him.  Otherwise, I usually leave Nemesis out as an unneeded complication, but when I saw Akash'Bhuta's HP total (and didn't yet know about Primordial Limbs), I made sure to encourage someone else in the party to play Argent.  And when I took on the Chairman, I knew he was supposed to be tough, so I made sure Mr. Fixit was there.

Ra vs. the Ennead seems unwise to me.  I haven't played against them, but just knowing that there are nine of them and only one of you, and their turn is first…30 HP isn't so many that I'd feel terribly safe in that bout.  I find it odd that there isn't really a hero whose shtick (as in their power and everything) is protecting other heroes.  It seems like there ought to be one "healer" or "guardian" type character, but while Fanatic and Legacy and Argent all dabble in this, they don't do all that much of it.  Absent such a character, playing a Nemesis against the more aggressive villains seems unsafe, but it can definitely help against the tough ones.  Knowing that Apostate is much harder to kill than 66 base HP would suggest, I'll definitely be bringing Fanatic (and at least three other heroes, instead of a 3-man band without her) next time I go up against him.  Heck, I might go the whole hog and play Legacy/Fanatic just to really try and put him down hard.  The manual says he's only a 2 but I don't believe that as yet.  Maybe he just had an absolutely perfect draw that first time.
